cards.front: On a velocity-time graph, what is on the horizontal axis?
On a velocity-time graph, what is on the vertical axis?
If a journey starts from rest, what is the initial velocity?
When velocity never goes below zero, its size is the [ ___ ].
cards.back: When velocity never goes below zero, its size is the speed.

cards.front: What shape shows constant acceleration on a velocity-time graph?
What does a horizontal section mean for acceleration?
On a velocity-time graph, what does a falling straight line represent if forward is positive?
On a velocity-time graph, acceleration is found from the [ ___ ].
cards.back: On a velocity-time graph, acceleration is found from the gradient.

cards.front: What is the formula for acceleration from a velocity-time graph section?
What are the units of acceleration?
The height of a velocity-time graph gives which quantity?
The [ ___ ] under a velocity-time graph gives displacement.
cards.back: The area under a velocity-time graph gives displacement.

cards.front: When does distance equal displacement on a velocity-time graph?
cards.back: When there is no area below the time axis.

cards.front: For displacement, what does area below the time axis represent?
How do you find total distance if part of a velocity-time graph is below the time axis?
What units result from area under a velocity-time graph, using seconds and $\text{m s}^{-1}$?
The area of a triangular velocity-time section is [ ___ ].
cards.back: The area of a triangular velocity-time section is $\frac{1}{2}\times\text{base}\times\text{height}$.

cards.front: A trapezium area is [ ___ ], where $a$ and $b$ are parallel sides.
cards.back: A trapezium area is $\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h$, where $a$ and $b$ are parallel sides.

cards.front: A tram goes from rest to $18\text{ m s}^{-1}$ in $30\text{ s}$. What is its acceleration?
A car accelerates for $8\text{ s}$, then drives at constant speed for $12\text{ s}$. When does deceleration begin?
For the same change in velocity, a larger acceleration magnitude means a [ ___ ] time.
cards.back: For the same change in velocity, a larger acceleration magnitude means a shorter time.

cards.front: A car accelerates from rest to $V$ in $8\text{ s}$. Its deceleration magnitude is twice as large. How long does braking from $V$ to rest take?
